title: Ships upon the Natal Water…
text:
Ships upon the natal water.
+
+Black water, animal of oblivion. Lilac water, sole wakefulness.
+
+The sunlit mystery of voices in the park. Oh so ancient.
editorial_note: Natal water keeps birth, origin, and fluidity together; black oblivion and lilac wakefulness remain opposed in the poem’s incantatory nominal phrases.

title: Falling
text:
Never again hope
+
+in a coming and going
+
+of names, of figures.
+
+Someone dreamed very badly,
+
+someone consumed by mistake
+
+the forgotten distances.
editorial_note: The indefinite alguien is repeated without identity; distance becomes a substance accidentally consumed, leaving hope outside the traffic of names and forms.

title: Naked, Dreaming a Solar Night…
text:
Naked, dreaming a solar night.
+
+I have lain through animal days.
+
+The wind and rain erased me
+
+as they would a fire, as they would a poem
+
+written on a wall.
editorial_note: Animal days retains the source’s compressed strangeness; the added pronoun in the erasure clarifies English agency without weakening the equivalence of body, fire, and wall-poem.

title: Farewell
text:
An abandoned fire kills its light.
+
+A bird in love raises its song.
+
+So many ravenous creatures in my silence
+
+and this little rain that keeps me company.
editorial_note: The first two inversions are resolved without changing their subjects; the vast appetite inside silence is answered only by the intimate smallness of rain.

title: In the Night beside You…
text:
In the night beside you
+
+words are codes, they are keys.
+
+the desire to die is king.
+
+
+May your body always be
+
+a beloved space of revelations.
editorial_note: Claves and llaves become codes and keys to preserve their distinction; the lowercase enthronement of death remains inside an otherwise tender bodily revelation.

title: Rescue
text: And it is always the lilac garden on the other side of the river. If the soul asks whether it is far away, it will be answered: on the other side of the river, not this one but that one.
editorial_note: The repeated other side is kept exact: rescue remains perpetually across not merely a river but the other, unreachable river.

title: The Only Wound
text:
What beast felled by astonishment
+
+crawls through my blood
+
+and wants to save itself?
+
+
+Here is what is difficult:
+
+to walk through the streets
+
+and point to the sky or the earth.
editorial_note: Caída de pasmo becomes felled by astonishment, holding shock and wonder together; the inner beast’s rescue contrasts with the ordinary impossibility of pointing outward.

text:
no more the sweet metamorphoses of a silken girl
+
+now sleepwalking on the ledge of fog
+
+her awakening of a breathing hand
+
+of a flower opening to the wind
editorial_note: The final de phrases remain grammatically suspended, allowing awakening to take the forms of a breathing hand and a flower opening into wind.
